# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** 11 years old  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c22 P1](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0001), [v2 c27 P61](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0061)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007)</sub>
- **Origin:** The United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c7 P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>

## Appearance

Paul has dark blue eyes and a small, delicate, sensitive face framed in chestnut curls. Although eleven years old, he is small for his age and looks closer to eight. He grows noticeably taller during his time in Avonlea and begins to look very much like his father.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v2 c28 P9](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0009)_

## Personality

Paul is a dreamy, highly imaginative child with a sober, reflective demeanor that makes his spirit seem older than his body. He possesses a gentle, refined nature and a subtle, poetic insight that sets him apart from other children. Despite his quiet, visionary thoughts, he is manly, fair-minded, and well-liked by his schoolmates. He holds strong affectionate ties to his family and teachers, though he experiences occasional flashes of uncanny insight into others.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v2 c27 P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030), [v2 c27 P54](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0054)_

## History

Paul Irving moved from the United States to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, in Avonlea. Upon entering Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized his poetic nature and imagination. He invented imaginary characters known as his 'rock people' and shared his thoughts with Anne. After hearing Anne praise Paul, Davy Keith was inspired to improve his own habits. Anne later introduced Paul to Miss Lavendar Lewis, with whom he instantly connected over shared romantic fancies. After Paul wrote to his father about visiting Miss Lavendar, Stephen Irving came to Avonlea, reunited with Miss Lavendar, and married her. Following the wedding, Paul prepared to move to Boston with his father and new stepmother.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P33](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0033), [v2 c11 P41](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0041), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c28 P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021), [v2 c28 P71](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0071), [v2 c29 P1](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0001), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- Born to Stephen Irving and his late wife  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c15 P2](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0002), [v2 c15 P8](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0008)</sub>

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I love him the best in all the world, and Grandma Irving next, and then you, teacher. I’d love you next to father if it wasn’t my duty to love Grandma Irving best, because she’s doing so much for me.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> We’re both that kind. You know, teacher. Isn’t it splendid to be that kind, teacher?  <sub>[v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019)</sub>

> Mrs. Lynde, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.  <sub>[v2 c19 P22](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0022)</sub>

> I knew I could trust father to pick me out a nice little second mother. It’s a fine thing to have a father you can depend on, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c29 P2](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0002)</sub>
